page.title_tag: 10-minute high-protein breakfasts for busy mornings | iEatz Healthy
page.meta_description: Five breakfasts you can make in ten minutes, each with 20g of protein or more, from things already in your kitchen. Full recipes, times and servings.
page.h1: What can I make for breakfast in 10 minutes?
page.direct_answer: Cottage cheese toast, savory oats with a jammy egg, a frozen-berry yogurt bowl, a black bean and egg skillet, or a peanut banana shake—each one 20 grams of protein or more, from things already in most kitchens. All five are written out in full below, with times, servings and where the protein comes from.

recipes.name: Whipped cottage cheese toast with chili crisp

image.alt: Whipped cottage cheese toast topped with chili crisp and flaky salt
image.pin_description: Whipped cottage cheese toast with chili crisp. 5 minutes, 28g protein.

ingredients: 1 thick slice sourdough or seeded bread
1 tsp chili crisp or hot honey
steps: Toast the bread dark. Dark toast holds up under a wet topping.
Blitz the cottage cheese for 20 seconds in a small blender, or mash it hard with a fork, until it turns glossy.
Pile it on the toast, spoon the chili crisp over, finish with flaky salt.
recipes.why_it_works: Cottage cheese whipped is a different food than cottage cheese scooped. Same tub, no shopping trip, 28 grams of protein.

recipes.name: Savory oats with a jammy egg

image.alt: Savory oats topped with a halved jammy egg, scallion and black pepper
image.pin_description: Savory oats with a 7-minute egg. 10 minutes, 24g protein.

steps: Boil water in a small pot. Lower one egg in for 7 minutes, then move it to cold water.
Add the oats to the same water and cook 5 minutes, stirring, until thick.
Stir in the cheese and a splash of soy. Top with the peeled egg, halved, plus scallion and a lot of pepper.
recipes.why_it_works: Oats are only a sweet food by habit. Treated like risotto they carry cheese, egg and salt, and the pot count stays at one.

recipes.name: Freezer-berry yogurt bowl with toasted seeds

image.alt: Greek yogurt bowl with warm frozen berries and toasted pumpkin seeds
image.pin_description: Frozen berries make their own syrup. 6 minutes, 26g protein.

steps: Toast the seeds dry in a small pan, 3 minutes, until they start popping.
Microwave the frozen berries 45 seconds so they collapse into their own syrup.
Spoon the berries over the yogurt, add the seeds and cinnamon, drizzle honey.
recipes.why_it_works: Frozen berries make their own sauce, which is the part a fresh berry cannot do. This is also the cheapest 26 grams on the list.

recipes.name: Black bean and egg skillet, wrapped

image.alt: Black bean and egg skillet with two tortillas rolled and cut in half
image.pin_description: One pan, one can. 9 minutes, 22g protein, feeds two.

ingredients: Salsa, cheese, cilantro — whatever is open
steps: Warm the beans in a dry skillet with the cumin, smashing about half of them.
Push them aside, crack the eggs into the empty half, cover, 3 minutes.
Warm the tortillas over the same burner, fill, add salsa, roll tight.
recipes.why_it_works: One pan, one can, and the can was already in the cupboard. It doubles for two people without doubling the time.

recipes.name: Peanut banana shake, no protein powder

image.alt: Peanut butter and banana protein shake in a tall glass beside a blender
image.pin_description: 21g of protein, no powder. Four minutes.

ingredients: 1/2 cup cottage cheese or Greek yogurt
steps: Put everything in the blender, cottage cheese first so it sits against the blade.
Blend 45 seconds. Longer than feels necessary — that is what makes it smooth instead of grainy.
Salt it. A pinch of salt is the difference between this and a sad smoothie.
recipes.why_it_works: Twenty-one grams of protein with nothing bought from a supplement aisle. Freeze bananas as they turn and this is a four-minute breakfast forever.

page.inline_app_mention: Every recipe on this page starts with a shopping list. The iEatz app starts with your fridge instead—name three things you already have and it writes the rest.

supporting_sections.heading: Where the protein actually comes from
supporting_sections.body: None of these use powder. In every case one ingredient is doing most of the work, which is useful to know because it is the ingredient worth keeping stocked.

faq.q: What is the fastest high-protein breakfast?
faq.a: The peanut banana shake, at about four minutes and 21 grams of protein. Everything goes in the blender at once and there is nothing to wash but the jar.

faq.q: Can I make any of these the night before?
faq.a: The savory oats and the yogurt bowl both hold. Cook the oats and refrigerate them, then loosen with a splash of water in the morning. For the yogurt bowl, keep the toasted seeds in a separate jar so they stay crisp.

faq.q: How do I get to 30 grams of protein at breakfast?
faq.a: Add one thing rather than making a bigger portion. An extra egg, two tablespoons of hemp seeds, or half a cup of cottage cheese each add roughly six to twelve grams without changing the recipe or the timing.
